findings.summary: Luna marked the accessible dinner menu partial and catalogued only 18 dinner products, while the official PDF contains many additional charcuterie choices, tapas, large plates, desserts, and drinks.

No restaurant-issued allergen matrix, complete ingredient list, negative allergen claim, may-contain statement, or cross-contact statement was found. The dinner allergy notice is a service instruction, not allergen evidence.

The frozen baseline includes category corruption and parser artifacts: wine-table fragments, regional/producer terms, and headings were captured as products; several food entries were classified as Desserts.

Frozen Gambas al Ajillo declares fish, but the reopened restaurant-issued menu names shrimp and supports shellfish, not fish. Frozen Lomo Ibérico declares tree nut with no current restaurant-issued support.
Officially linked brunch and full-wine-list PDFs could not be retrieved, so their current scope and any historical baseline matches remain unverifiable.

verifier.summary: Independent verification found material scope, extraction, and baseline-allergen discrepancies. Dinner and happy-hour sources reopened; brunch and bottle-menu sources remain inaccessible. Luna omitted many current dinner products, and the frozen catalog includes artifacts and unsupported/misclassified allergen claims.
